notes.title: New Opening Sequence & Enhanced Base Building Experience
notes.content:
[p]It’s been a while since we sent an update, but with good reason. We’ve been working hard on revamping many of the core mechanics from last year’s PAX prototype, and work is going well. We intend to reveal all soon, but for now here’s a taster:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44417058/7ffa0a785cde8e9e5c167cb4d3588977e75e8b1c.png"][/img][/p][h1][b]NEW OPENING[/b][/h1][p]We decided to strip back the original opening sequence of the game. In the previous version you would have started on the Moon with the basics of a base already built (a hub, a landing pad and a road connecting them). But we realized in testing that this meant players often didn’t feel like they were truly building the base.
[/p][p]So we took the timeline back a bit and started with the first landing. In the new version, you start from the point of the 1st lander descending to the surface of Shackleton Crater and deploying your very first rover. That rover proceeds to do beginner-level tasks like scanning areas for further development, allowing your second rover to start clearing and preparing the area.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44417058/e762a5f0cc7b5640256f71564b291bf0d9f19753.png"][/img][/p][p]The purpose behind these steps is to help you understand how aspects of the game like ordering and control work more clearly, and to give you more of a sense of beginning. After your first lander comes a second, this time with new rovers and new functions: Now you can print, now you can build. Now you can start to see your base take shape.[/p][p][/p][p]This leads to a first major task: building a landing pad. Most lunar engineering experts consider this a highly important step in the construction of any base because it is the gateway that allows more complicated and fragile spacecraft to land and be deployed. So too with your first pad, which allows, after all the landers, for the first rocket in history to land on the moon.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44417058/8672c5efb247ffbcadb944d55a8c0484058c08a6.png"][/img][/p][p]From there you are on your way to colonization and industrialization. You can set up your base, create structures for energy, habitation, mining and development and start to expand your footprint! [/p]

notes.title: Expanded Map Coverage
notes.content:
We’d like to share some of our recent progress, as well as a deep dive into some of the challenges we’re overcoming while developing Possible One. One of our most demanding tasks has been building a massive grid map. As you expand your base across the entire Shackleton region and search for exotic resources, we’re managing more than 450,000 separate grid tiles—a scale that tests our game systems to their limits, but also offers incredible opportunities for exploration and strategy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44417058/ba170b97d8348927590af65a89eaba5aef264ebb.jpg[/img]

[b]Working with Huge Map Tiles[/b]
Handling such a large grid comes with several challenges, the most obvious being how to render it all at once. To address this, we developed a system that only displays what’s near your camera. We also introduced a “pooling system” that hides unused items and reuses them when you move, eliminating the need to create new assets for every single tile.

[b]Efficient Data Access[/b]
Each tile in Possible One contains resources, construction details, pathfinding data, and more. To keep things running smoothly, we rely on a specialized “Hash Table” keyed to each tile’s location. This allows instant data retrieval without slowing down performance—even across the entire Shackleton region.

[b]Managing Memory & Save Files[/b]
Without a careful approach, storing information for over 450,000 tiles would be overwhelming. Our solution is straightforward: default values aren’t stored in memory. By treating each tile as “Dirt” initially and only saving changes (like when you build a “Road”), we dramatically cut memory usage. Combined with procedural algorithms and file compression, we’ve slashed memory needs by a factor of a thousand and keep save files speedy!.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44417058/8b3ec263f93d4677074e27c0f545aa83fe8335a4.jpg[/img]

[b]Thank You for Your Support[/b]
Once again, we’d like to extend our thanks once more to everyone who has provided input—it has already had a drastic impact. your feedback is essential to making Possible One: Lunar Industries more engaging and intuitive. We’ll continue to share updates as we work on further improvements.

notes.title: Dynamic AI Crew Management
notes.content:
We’re excited to introduce a significant enhancement to Possible One’s lunar management experience: a dynamic new AI system that brings a new level of realism and challenge to your colony. This advanced AI integrates a range of statuses, requirements, and reactions among your crew, all shifting in response to your management style. You’ll need to build, assign, and adapt strategically to keep your astronauts efficient!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44417058/e7a695f429c41b1fcef99ed2b12693e07f965b0a.png[/img]

Manage your astronauts’ health, stress, and other vital stats capable of changing based on their working conditions and the quality of your base’s infrastructure. For example, a stressed astronaut is more prone to work-related injuries, and lacking proper facilities can disrupt their work. Meanwhile, without a dedicated cafeteria, crew members will resort to eating in less ideal environments, causing their morale to decline over time.

Once again, we’d like to thank everyone who has provided input—your feedback is essential to making Possible One: Lunar Industries more engaging and intuitive. We’ll continue to share updates as we work on further improvements.

notes.title: Streamlined Ordering and Vehicle Menu
notes.content:
We’ve been hard at work to make sure Possible One: Lunar Industries provides a groundbreaking lunar base-building experience! We're thrilled to announce major improvements to our construction and command systems: a streamlined Ordering and Vehicle Menu. Based on valuable feedback from our time showing off the game at PAX West 2024, we’ve redesigned the interface for a smoother, more intuitive experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44417058/71bf664546c519339f76c7b61a58d979eb289735.jpg[/img]

The new menu is designed to expand from the bottom of the screen with each selection, providing a clear, step-by-step approach to commands. This unified menu now covers both ordering and vehicle management, simplifying navigation and enhancing accessibility. Essential commands, such as Demolish and Scout, are now integrated directly into this interface, allowing for seamless transitions between different actions!

We extend our thanks to everyone who provided input—your feedback is essential to making Possible One: Lunar Industries more engaging and intuitive. We’ll continue to share updates as we work on further improvements.
